svg.title: Maknae fs.read boundary crossings
svg.desc: UML sequence diagram of the Maknae fs.read path across the trust boundary.
svg.text: One request, end to end. The OS appears TWICE because that is the whole of ADR-0009: the daemon asks only where the object is, and
only the subject's own re-open performs the read. Each step names the code that implements it.
O_PATH on Linux: no access is conferred and none is checked on the object
4. Request{Read} + SCM_RIGHTS(fd) over the mTLS plane
confinement beneath home, nlink == 1, regular file
21. bytes to stdout, after the acknowledged Success
A failed open still sends, UNARMED. The daemon then has no descriptor and refuses it before the PDP: read descriptor missing.
recvmsg, never read(2): a plain read silently DESTROYS the attached descriptor.
A malformed path is BadRequest — no authorization decision is reached at all.
Reads the daemon's OWN fd table (/proc/self/fd). Needs no permission on the object's directories — which is why a 0700 home still works. A descriptor that confers access is refused.
Built on the KERNEL-REPORTED path, never the string the client sent — so the deny list evaluates the object, not an alias for it (ADR-0009 D6).

THE SEAM, and the only crossing on this diagram that is not a process boundary — an in-process trait-object call on a spawn_blocking worker. maknae-authz-basic is what a deployment swaps to change the decision model (ADR-0004); maknae-authz-dcs would sit here.

Composition runs in the KERNEL, not the backend: deny-overrides is the daemon's rule, so no backend can waive another's Deny. fs.read is decided only on the local lane, and never on an OS preapproval.
No grant without a durable intent. No trail, no read.
The OS decides the read HERE, as the subject. The fresh fd is bound to the held object (dev/ino, nlink == 1, path, size ≤ max_bytes) before a byte is read.
Content is released only once its completion record is durable. The daemon never read it.
